newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Short-staffed Cyprus leisure spots set to strike.
newsitem.headline: Short-staffed Cyprus leisure spots set to strike.

text.p: Dozens of short-staffed restaurants at the most popular holiday spot in Cyprus will shut down next week to protest against a government ban on issuing work permits to foreigners, owners warned on Wednesday.

Leisure spots, which are mainly restaurants, will stay shut from Monday onwards in the Ayia Napa and Protaras resorts on the Mediterranean island's south east, their industry association said in a statement.
Owners say the only solution to what they have described as an acute labour shortage is to employ foreigners to do certain jobs, since they cannot find local staff.
Some establishments have been unable to resume operations after the winter break because of the labour shortage, they say.
The government has halted the issue of work permits to foreigners in the leisure industry until June, after representations by workers' unions.

Trade unions see the employment of foreign workers as a last resort to cope with any shortages on the local labour market, and have expressed concerns in the past that cheap foreign labour has cost Cypriots their jobs.
While not overlooking the reluctance of Cypriots in getting a job in the sector, trade unions blame it on the owners.
"There have been cases where owners don't abide by the terms of collective working agreements" said Yiannakis Phillipou of PEO trade union.
